messages:
Marta: Ran the daily trace playback for model-foo-8k vs prod. p95 is ~7% worse in playback. Looks like KV cache warmup is the main diff, plus different kernel picked for attention on a subset. Anyone seen this pattern before?
infra-bot: deploy-checker: playback job finished (id=playback-2026-05-01-01) :white_check_mark:
Ben: Can you paste the playback config + the backend kernel hints you used?
Marta: Sure. Command: `./trace_playback --trace s3://prod-traces/2026-04-30/ --model model-foo-8k --seed 42 --preserve-order --anonymize uids` 
Marta: Config snippet:
```
{"sampling_rate":0.06,"preserve_order":true,"simulate_kv_ttl":false,"kernel_override":null}
```
Kai: Two quick things: 1) anonymization currently hashes user ids into buckets which changes request spreading -> different KV warming. 2) kernel selection is non-deterministic if we let the runtime autotuner run — playback may hit a different kernel for short sequences.
Olivia: That matches. On prod we see kv_hit_rate ~0.78 on warm runs; in playback kv_hit_rate ~0.41. Without simulating prior requests that populate KV, the runtime will choose kernels optimized for cold-cache costs which can bump latency.
Ben: OK. Proposed experiments (short runs): A) force kernel to XLA-attn-v2 (same as prod) B) enable simulate_kv_ttl + prewarm window (replay last 5m before test) C) keep request order + original timestamps D) increase sampling seed to match distribution. Anyone object?
Marta: No objections. I'll run A and B now and post numbers.
perf-bot: quick-profile: run=playback-A; p50=48ms p95=210ms cpu=3.1 GPUms=4200 kv_hit=0.44 kernel=XLA-attn-v1
perf-bot: quick-profile: run=playback-B; p50=40ms p95=165ms cpu=2.6 GPUms=3800 kv_hit=0.76 kernel=XLA-attn-v2
Kai: Nice — B reduced p95 a lot and bumped kv_hit to prod-like. Suggest we add deterministic hashing for anonymize that preserves per-user session locality (hash -> consistent bucket) and a replay prewarm stage that replays preceding N seconds to warm caches.
Olivia: Also add a parity check: compare token-level outputs for a small batch with and without simulate_kv_ttl + kernel_override to ensure no unintended behavior changes. Use SSE/sha256 on outputs.
Ben: Action items: Marta to add deterministic anon + prewarm in harness (ETA today), Kai to add kernel override flag + test matrix, Olivia to add parity checksum step. We'll reconvene after runs. :thumbsup:
Marta: Logging plan: I'll attach run artifacts (kv metrics, kernel traces, stdout logs) to the ticket `INFR-4682`.
Ben: Thanks — this is a good apples-to-apples recipe for future perf regressions.
